subheading: CLINICAL FEATURES OF AN UNCONSCIOUS PATIENT
subheading_corrected: CLINICAL FEATURES OF AN UNCONSCIOUS PATIENT
text:
CLINICAL FEATURES OF AN UNCONSCIOUS PATIENT
- Varying levels of impaired consciousness:
- Comatose: no response to stimulus, however painful
- Semi-comatose: some response to pain
- Stuporous: a state deeper than sleep; vigorous stimulation required to
stimulate response
- Other features:
- Cessation of respiration or abnormal ventilatory patterns: Cheyne-
Stokes, ataxic, apneustic, gasping etc
- Unresponsiveness or variable response to painful stimuli
- Features of the underlying cause(s)
- Stroke: may present with hemiparesis, facial asymmetry, crossed-eye
defects, speech defects etc.
- Epilepsy: frothing or tongue biting; abrasions of the extremities;
positive past history
- Infections: may present with fever, neck stiffness
- Drug overdosage/toxins: pin-point pupils; respiratory problems;
suggestive history
- Uraemia: characteristic fetor; skin rashes; oedema; severe dehydration
- Head trauma: haematoma; subconjuctival haemorrhage
- Bleeding from orifices (if coma is due to trauma or bleeding diathesis)
- Features of raised intracranial pressure:
- Slow pulse (Cushing's reflex); rising blood pressure; papilloedema
